pages.text: $(thing)Computability$()$(br2)Turing imagined the simplest machine that can compute anything, and proved it cannot always tell whether it will ever stop.

$(thing)Insight$(): 110$(br2)$(thing)Builds on$(): Algorithms, Formal Logic.$(br2)$(thing)Samples$(): 2 Proof Certificate.$(br2)$(thing)Derivation$(): Count the Turing machines with n states that read and write two symbols: each state and symbol needs a symbol to write, a way to move and a next state (or halt). Write how many machines N there are.
